newsitem.title: UK: Sterling debt and futures closing report.
newsitem.headline: Sterling debt and futures closing report.

text.p: Gilts chalked up solid gains in a day of thin volumes as German Bunds set the pace in Europe, dealers said.
The June gilt future ended 12/32 ahead at 109-01 while the June Bund leapt almost a full point as a fresh wave of optimism about European economic and monetary union gripped the market.

"It's been a quiet day but we have been dragged up by Germany," said a senior gilts salesman. "I saw no selling whatsoever at the lower levels and now non-farm payrolls are out of the way, gilts should push ahead."
June gilts dropped as low as 108-15 before recovering.
U.S. jobs data, released last Friday, had stopped the bond markets. Gilts, having hit a floor last Tuesday and then traded sideways have consolidated enough to recover, the salesman said.
"With sterling so strong, gilts are looking very cheap relative to Germany," the salesman said. The gilt/Bund spread has widened to 186 points from 178 last week.
Sterling shot up on Monday, above its old exchange rate mechanism floor of 2.7780 marks and is now up 22 percent on the mark since last August.
But Steve Scott, gilts analyst at Kleinwort Benson, said that could actually hurt the UK market.

"If sterling carries on going up and people expect base rates to rise more quickly and by a larger amount than they did before, then there's a danger overseas investors will take profits in gilts," he said.
June short sterling futures closed unchanged at 93.30, pricing in a half-point rate rise in the first half of the year.

Tuesday is set to be another quiet day with Wednesday enlivened by the release of manufacturing output data and the monthly monetary meeting of Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George following on Thursday.
Not one analyst expects rate to rise before the election and a forecast of only a modest 0.3 percent increase in February manufacturing output could give Clarke another excuse to hold fire.
